item.title: Pain in Spain: Why former Liverpool team-mates Trent Alexander-Arnold and Harvey Elliott might not last long in La Liga
item.description: Trent & Elliott's struggles.jpg - Getty/GOAL Neither player's move to Spain is working out particularly well, meaning both could be on the bench at Mestalla on Saturday night - if they're lucky Trent Alexander-Arnold and Harvey Elliott haven't played on the same pitch since the final few minutes of Liverpool's 1-1 draw with Crystal Palace on May 25 of last year. It was a day of mixed emotions for both boyhood fans of the Reds. Alexander-Arnold had already gone public with his difficult decision to leave Liverpool on a free transfer, while it was clear that Elliott's days on Merseyside were also numbered after a season spent playing the role of super-sub. However, neither man could have hoped to bow out in more celebratory circumstances, as Arne Slot's Liverpool were presented with the Premier League trophy after the game at a jubilant Anfield. That joyous occasion might well come up if Elliott and Alexander-Arnold get a chance to chat at Mestalla on Saturday evening, before or after the Liga meeting between their respective new clubs, Valencia and Real Madrid. As it stands, though, the chances of them actually getting to share a field again are slim at best, as neither player's spell in Spain is going according to plan at all... Fantastic first impression The Englishman surprised the Madrid - and Liverpool - media by speaking Spanish in his first press conference Of the two former team-mates, Alexander-Arnold was obviously expected to make the bigger impact in La Liga. Alexander-Arnold had won pretty much all there was to win at Liverpool and, in doing so, had established himself as arguably the most exciting right-back in world football. He wasn't satisfied, though, and not even the probability of becoming club captain after Virgil van Dijk's eventual departure could convince him to stay at Anfield beyond the summer of 2025. Alexander-Arnold wanted to redefine the role of right-back and, whatever one might think about his defensive deficiencies, he unquestionably had the attacking game to excel at the Santiago Bernabeu. Madrid certainly concurred, and they were so desperate to bring him on board that they even agreed to pay Liverpool £8.3 million ($11.1m) for a player with just one month left on his contract so that they could have him for the Club World Cup. Alexander-Arnold also made a fantastic first impression at his new club by speaking Spanish at his official unveiling as a Madrid player , but despite mastering a language that his team-mate, compatriot and good friend Jude Bellingham is still struggling with, the defender has not settled anywhere near as seamlessly into his new surroundings. item.content:encoded: Trent & Elliott's struggles.jpg - Getty/GOAL Neither player's move to Spain is working out particularly well, meaning both could be on the bench at Mestalla on Saturday night - if they're lucky Trent Alexander-Arnold and Harvey Elliott haven't played on the same pitch since the final few minutes of Liverpool's 1-1 draw with Crystal Palace on May 25 of last year. It was a day of mixed emotions for both boyhood fans of the Reds. Alexander-Arnold had already gone public with his difficult decision to leave Liverpool on a free transfer, while it was clear that Elliott's days on Merseyside were also numbered after a season spent playing the role of super-sub. However, neither man could have hoped to bow out in more celebratory circumstances, as Arne Slot's Liverpool were presented with the Premier League trophy after the game at a jubilant Anfield. That joyous occasion might well come up if Elliott and Alexander-Arnold get a chance to chat at Mestalla on Saturday evening, before or after the Liga meeting between their respective new clubs, Valencia and Real Madrid. As it stands, though, the chances of them actually getting to share a field again are slim at best, as neither player's spell in Spain is going according to plan at all... Fantastic first impression The Englishman surprised the Madrid - and Liverpool - media by speaking Spanish in his first press conference Of the two former team-mates, Alexander-Arnold was obviously expected to make the bigger impact in La Liga. Alexander-Arnold had won pretty much all there was to win at Liverpool and, in doing so, had established himself as arguably the most exciting right-back in world football. He wasn't satisfied, though, and not even the probability of becoming club captain after Virgil van Dijk's eventual departure could convince him to stay at Anfield beyond the summer of 2025. Alexander-Arnold wanted to redefine the role of right-back and, whatever one might think about his defensive deficiencies, he unquestionably had the attacking game to excel at the Santiago Bernabeu. Madrid certainly concurred, and they were so desperate to bring him on board that they even agreed to pay Liverpool £8.3 million ($11.1m) for a player with just one month left on his contract so that they could have him for the Club World Cup. Alexander-Arnold also made a fantastic first impression at his new club by speaking Spanish at his official unveiling as a Madrid player , but despite mastering a language that his team-mate, compatriot and good friend Jude Bellingham is still struggling with, the defender has not settled anywhere near as seamlessly into his new surroundings. 'It hurts me' Jose Mourinho says he feels bad about relegating Alexander-Arnold to the role of third-choice right-back at Madrid Alexander-Arnold stated in his first press conference that he couldn't wait to "show [his game], win many titles and become a champion" - but he's not realised any of those goals yet. There are, of course, some mitigating circumstances. Alexander-Arnold's first season in Spain was repeatedly interrupted by injuries, thus preventing him from building up any momentum. A change of coach didn't help either, with Xabi Alonso sacked in January and replaced by the hapless Alvaro Arbeloa. Only now, under Jose Mourinho, are Madrid starting to look like a stable side again. The thing is, though, while 'The Special One' has, for the time being at least, proven a positive development for Los Blancos, it's been nothing but negative for Alexander-Arnold. He moved to Madrid with the intention of proving himself the best right-back of all time - but Mourinho doesn't even think he's the second-best right-back at the Bernabeu, with Denzel Dumfries and, even more gallingly, midfielder Federico Valverde both ahead of him in the pecking order. Mourinho has expressed some sympathy for the unexpectedly dire situation Alexander-Arnold now finds himself in, but that doesn't mean he's going to do anything to help him find a way out of it. "It hurts me. I don't like making players feel bad; I prefer them to feel good," Mourinho told reporters . "When you build a squad with two players per position and end up playing a third (Valverde), it's not something I appreciate... "But there are things more important than these feelings, things that matter more for the team at a given moment. I felt we needed to change our midfield and play Fede in that position. It was a decision made for the team, not based on individual players." Alexander-Arnold did, at least, play the entirety of last weekend's 3-0 victory over Racing Santander but it was just his fourth start of the Liga season, and came after getting just one minute of game time in the Clasico win over Barcelona at Camp Nou. He was also an unused substitute for the third Champions League game in a row in midweek, as Madrid maintained their good run of form by picking up all three points from their trip to Greece to face AEK Athens thanks to a late goal from Valverde. As a result, it's difficult to know whether he'll see any action at all against Valencia - or be once again left sitting on the bench. Unfortunately for Elliott, there's no guarantee whether he'll even be included in Javier Aguirre's matchday squad. From bad to worse? Elliott had a nightmare loan spell at Villa Park, and his stay at Mestalla has started disastrously When Elliott joined Aston Villa on loan from Liverpool last summer, with a view to a permanent transfer, it looked like one of those rare deals that suits everyone involved. As it transpired, nobody benefited, least of all Elliott, who essentially lost an entire year of his career because Unai Emery didn't want a player signed by former sporting director Monchi. The coach couldn't fault Elliott for effort or professionalism. He just didn't think he was worth £35m ($47m), so the two-time Under-21 European champions was prevented from making 10 Premier League appearances for Villa, as that would have triggered the obligation-to-buy clause in his contract. It was a complete farce, one that Emery admitted was incredibly unfair on Elliott. "I feel sorry for the boy," the Spaniard said. Crazy as it may seem, though, there's a case to be made that Elliott's move to Mestalla has actually been even more damaging - at least from a reputational perspective. After arriving in Valencia on deadline day, the 23-year-old has been involved in six Liga games - but started none of them. Worse still, he was sent off just 19 minutes after coming on in the 2-1 loss to Villarreal on October 21 after picking up two bookings in quick succession for dissent - much to the understandably fury of Aguirre, who replaced Carlos Corberan as the club's permanent coach the month before. "I don't know what he could have said to the referee, he barely speaks Spanish," the former Mexico coach said, "so getting sent off for something he said just makes me angry. It's an absurd, ridiculous dismissal, and I told him as much." As a result of his red card, Elliott was banned for last weekend's game against Elche, and given 19th-placed Valencia picked up their first win since the middle of September without him, it seems he'll see few minutes - if any - against Madrid. Indeed, amid reports that Elliott arrived in Spain in poor physical condition, and has yet to register a goal or assist for Valencia, there is already talk of his loan stay being terminated during the winter transfer window, particularly as the sporting director that signed him, Ron Gourlay, was sacked on the same day as Corberan. Funnily enough, Alexander-Arnold is also being linked with a return to Liverpool in 2027, given he's 28 now and can ill-afford to spend the season as Madrid's third-choice right-back if he wants to keep his place in Thomas Tuchel's England squad. The word coming out of his camp is that he is determined to stay and fight for his place in Mourinho's team but, at this particular point in time, it actually does

item.title: Canadiens star Cole Caufield makes NHL history with more OT heroics to beat Mammoth
item.description: Eric Bolte-Imagn Images Canadiens star Cole Caufield makes NHL history with more OT heroics to beat Mammoth appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Cole Caufield and the Montreal Canadiens bounced back from a wild collapse in a big way , and the sniper made NHL history in the process. Caufield scored 30 seconds into overtime to lift Montreal to a 5-4 win over the Utah Mammoth at Bell Centre on Thursday night. The game-winner was Caufield’s 15th career overtime goal, and he got there faster than anyone in league history. The 25-year-old reached the mark in just 384 career games, beating Connor McDavid, who needed 559 games to get to 15. Overtime has long been Caufield’s specialty. Last season, he scored back-to-back overtime winners against the Seattle Kraken and Nashville Predators in October, and he reached 40 goals for the first time in his career with an overtime winner against the Boston Bruins in March . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Thursday’s goal was vintage Caufield. On a 2-on-1, the Canadiens forward faked a slap shot before ripping a wrist shot over the right shoulder of Mammoth goaltender Sebastian Cossa to send the Bell Centre crowd home happy. COLE CAUFIELD WINS IT IN OVERTIME 🔥🚨 pic.twitter.com/JAuuHUaQyW — B/R Open Ice (@BR_OpenIce) November 6, 2026 Montreal had to work for it. Utah’s Logan Cooley put on a show with three goals and an assist, recording his second hat trick in four games. Nick Schmaltz’s power-play goal gave the Mammoth a 4-3 lead early in the third period, but Adam Engstrom tied the game with 5:06 left in regulation to force overtime. Nick Suzuki made a strong return to the lineup after missing six games with an upper-body injury, finishing with a goal and two assists. Arber Xhekaj and Kirby Dach also scored for Montreal, and Jakub Dobes made 16 saves. The win was a much-needed response for the Canadiens. Just two nights earlier, Montreal blew a 4-0 lead in the final 2:39 of regulation and lost 5-4 in overtime to the Winnipeg Jets, marking the latest four-goal comeback in NHL history. Caufield had scored in that game, too. This time, he made sure the Canadiens came out on top in the extra period. Montreal improved to 10-3-3 on the season and has now won six of its last seven games. Utah, meanwhile, fell to 10-6-1. The Canadiens will look to keep the momentum going when they visit the Toronto Maple Leafs on Saturday. Related: Canadiens getting huge Nick Suzuki boost vs. Mammoth Related: Canadiens forward Ivan Demidov fractured ankle in preseason; agent provides injury update

item.title: Ducks land in CFP rankings despite rocky season
item.description: Oregon football’s season hasn’t worked out the way it expected. But the Ducks (5-3, 3-2 Big Ten) were ranked in the first College Football Playoff rankings. Oregon came in at No. 23 in the initial rankings, revealed live on ESPN on Tuesday. Dan Lanning’s team is on the outside looking in at the 12-team playoff, one season before a 24-team playoff is set to likely go into effect. The No. 23 Ducks are coming off a confidence-boosting win over Northwestern, heading on the road to face No. 12 Ohio State (6-2, 4-1) this Saturday. That matchup originally included the preseason Nos. 1 and 2 teams in the AP poll. But in this chaotic college football season, the Buckeyes are reeling after a road loss to No. 20 USC. Other Big Ten teams in this week’s CFP rankings include No. 19 Iowa, No. 8 UCLA and No. 4 Indiana. Latest Ducks news Eastern Washington vs. Oregon prediction, odds and best bets: Tony Stubblefield’s new-look Ducks host the Eagles Local long snapping prospect commits to Oregon football Experts release early Oregon-Ohio State predictions: Can Ducks play spoiler for Buckeyes’ CFP hopes? item.title: El Cerrito High's football program, coach suspended after hazing allegations involving 22 teammates
item.description: The El Cerrito High School football program has been suspended following a police investigation into allegations of hazing and bullying involving current and former players, school district officials said. The decision came after El Cerrito police disclosed that 22 current and former football players are under investigation. "Given what we now know about the scope of the law enforcement investigation, we must immediately suspend the program in order to make sure that there are no further harms to students," said Liz Sanders, assistant superintendent of communications for the West Contra Costa Unified School District. District officials said they first became aware of the allegations last month. "October 2nd is when we learned of these allegations and immediately referred them to law enforcement," Sanders said. According to El Cerrito police, the alleged incidents occurred between September 2024 and October 2026. "We've learned that approximately 22 subjects were involved in this hazing and bullying," said Capt. Lauren Caputo of the El Cerrito Police Department. "And we're investigating crimes of battery, sexual battery, stalking and other crimes." The El Cerrito High School football team won a state championship in 2025. Police said the alleged incidents occurred on school grounds and involved football players targeting their own teammates. "Our detectives initiated an investigation. During this investigation, they conducted numerous interviews of school staff, witnesses and also victims. Through those interviews, they were able to obtain some video evidence which further corroborated some of the allegations by the victims," said Caputo. The school district also confirmed that the head football coach has been placed on leave. "It is possible that a coach could face charges in this incident," Caputo said. Parents upset after football program suspended Parents and players at El Cerrito High School said they were shocked and frustrated after the West Contra Costa Unified School District suspended the football program amid a hazing and bullying investigation. Parents and players at El Cerrito High School said they were shocked and frustrated after the West Contra Costa Unified School District suspended the football program amid a hazing and bullying investigation. ABC7 Eyewitness News spoke with several parents who argued the entire program should not be punished before charges are filed. "People shouldn't be penalized for other people's actions," said Katrice West, whose son plays on the team. Parents said they have been seeking more information from the district for months. "The parents don't know nothing. They tell us as everyone else finds out," said Kandice Ward, another football parent. District officials said they first became aware of the allegations last month. "October 2nd is when we learned of these allegations and immediately referred them to law enforcement," Sanders said. According to El Cerrito police, the alleged incidents occurred between September 2024 and October 2026. "We've learned that approximately 22 subjects were involved in this hazing and bullying," said Capt. Lauren Caputo of the El Cerrito Police Department. "And we're investigating crimes of battery, sexual battery, stalking and other crimes." The El Cerrito High School football team won a state championship in 2025. Police said the alleged incidents occurred on school grounds and involved football players targeting their own teammates. "Our detectives initiated an investigation. During this investigation, they conducted numerous interviews of school staff, witnesses and also victims. Through those interviews, they were able to obtain some video evidence which further corroborated some of the allegations by the victims," said Caputo. The school district also confirmed that the head football coach has been placed on leave. "It is possible that a coach could face charges in this incident," Caputo said. Parents upset after football program suspended Parents and players at El Cerrito High School said they were shocked and frustrated after the West Contra Costa Unified School District suspended the football program amid a hazing and bullying investigation. Parents and players at El Cerrito High School said they were shocked and frustrated after the West Contra Costa Unified School District suspended the football program amid a hazing and bullying investigation. ABC7 Eyewitness News spoke with several parents who argued the entire program should not be punished before charges are filed. "People shouldn't be penalized for other people's actions," said Katrice West, whose son plays on the team. Parents said they have been seeking more information from the district for months. "The parents don't know nothing. They tell us as everyone else finds out," said Kandice Ward, another football parent. Players and parents noted that no arrests have been made and no charges have been filed. Some players also said certain individuals connected to the investigation have already been moved to independent study programs, though the district has not confirmed that information. "We're really not a bad group of kids," said El Cerrito football player Namon West IV. "I see a lot of my teammates. They work really hard in class to make sure they're good." Ward said her son had no involvement in the allegations and questioned why the entire program was suspended. "My son is a 4.0 student. He ain't have nothing to do with this, and you're taking the whole program away for what?" she said. Police said they expect charges to be filed as the investigation continues. item.title: Barcelona youth team defender makes major progress in recovery from knee injury
item.description: Barcelona youth team defender makes major progress in recovery from knee injury Barcelona have received encouraging news regarding Patricio Pacifico’s recovery, with the 20-year-old defender taking an important step towards returning to action after suffering a serious knee injury earlier this year. According to Mundo Deportivo , the Uruguayan has been discharged from the medical centre and has resumed working on the training pitches at the Ciutat Esportiva. Pacifico’s progress is actually a significant development for Barça Atletic, particularly given the lengthy recovery period initially anticipated following his injury. The defender is now entering a new phase of rehabilitation, with the possibility of returning to competitive action around February 2027, depending on how his recovery progresses. Pacifico makes important progress in Barcelona recovery Pacifico suffered a rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament in his left knee during Barcelona Atlètic’s match against UE Olot on April 19, 2026. He subsequently underwent successful surgery in May, with Barcelona initially estimating a recovery period of approximately 12 months. Patricio Pacifico has taken an important step in his recovery. (Picture credit: Instagram/@patridominguez8) This is why his latest progress is a significant milestone, as he has started working on the grass at the club’s training complex. On that note, the outlet mentions that the defender is currently using the sand pitch to strengthen his muscles before progressing to more demanding rehabilitation exercises. Barcelona defender targets return to ball work before January Pacifico’s rehabilitation will continue through several carefully managed stages. Once he completes his current strengthening programme, the next objective will be to begin jogging before gradually introducing changes of direction and increased running intensity. These steps will determine when he can safely return to ball work, which is expected to happen towards the end of December. If everything progresses as planned, the Uruguayan could subsequently begin reintegrating into group training between January and February. View this post on Instagram A post shared by FC Barcelona B (@fcbarcelonab) However, returning to full competitive action will depend on his physical condition and the medical staff’s assessment, meaning that the initial estimation of 12 months could be fulfilled. Barcelona maintain faith in Pacifico despite serious injury Barcelona’s decision to extend Pacifico’s loan from Defensor Sporting until the end of the 2026/27 season showed their continued confidence in his potential. Notably, the agreement retained the purchase option included in the original arrangement. Before suffering his injury, Pacifico had made seven appearances for Barça Atlètic, all as a starter. The original agreement stipulated that the purchase option would become mandatory after ten appearances, meaning he needs three more matches to trigger it.

item.title: Real Madrid face crucial €80 million decision next summer for 22-year-old former academy graduate
item.description: Real Madrid face crucial €80 million decision next summer for 22-year-old former academy graduate Real Madrid have done an excellent job of developing young academy talents and selling them to other clubs while retaining control over their futures. Los Blancos did this with Nico Paz a few seasons ago, selling him to Como but retaining buy-back clauses for each summer. Paz’s development at the Italian club reached a whole new level, prompting Los Blancos to buy him back this summer and sell him again to the Italian club for a huge fee. His current season at Como has turned him into a football superstar, and he has repeatedly been linked with another return to the Spanish capital. Now, according to Fabrizio Romano , Los Blancos have a limited window to exercise their €80 million buy-back clause next summer. Real Madrid have until summer 2027 to bring Paz back The important revelation from Romano was that Real Madrid only have the summer of 2027 to bring him back. After that, their buy-back clause expires, and Los Blancos will lose all control over the player’s future. Real Madrid’s buyback clause for Nico Paz expires in 2027. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) The arrangement was established last summer when Como agreed to pay €60 million to acquire the remaining rights to Paz, who wanted another season under Cesc Fabregas. Real Madrid somehow managed to include an option for the summer of 2027, and now they have a major decision to make. There is a chance that the Spanish club may have a right of first refusal beyond the summer of 2027, but that isn’t the same as having a favourable buy-back clause. A difficult decision awaits Real Madrid Paz has developed into the superstar around whom the Como team has been built. He scored twice and provided an assist in the Italian side’s historic 4-1 victory over Manchester United. Financially, Real Madrid should have no problem pulling off this deal. They would effectively need to spend only around €20 million extra to bring him back. Real Madrid still have some control on Nico Paz. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) Even if they decide to sell him on after that, the price is likely to be much higher than the buy-back clause, and Los Blancos stand to make a profit. However, bringing him back and finding a place for him in the squad would be a bigger challenge, given the kind of talent already at the club. Real Madrid already have Jude Bellingham, Arda Guler and Bernardo Silva in the squad, and not giving Paz minutes would not be ideal for his current trajectory. It remains to be seen how Real Madrid approach this situation and whether they pay the money to bring Paz back to the Santiago Bernabeu next summer.

There is a chance that the Spanish club may have a right of first refusal beyond the summer of 2027, but that isn’t the same as having a favourable buy-back clause. A difficult decision awaits Real Madrid Paz has developed into the superstar around whom the Como team has been built. He scored twice and provided an assist in the Italian side’s historic 4-1 victory over Manchester United. Financially, Real Madrid should have no problem pulling off this deal. They would effectively need to spend only around €20 million extra to bring him back. Real Madrid still have some control on Nico Paz. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) Even if they decide to sell him on after that, the price is likely to be much higher than the buy-back clause, and Los Blancos stand to make a profit. However, bringing him back and finding a place for him in the squad would be a bigger challenge, given the kind of talent already at the club. Real Madrid already have Jude Bellingham, Arda Guler and Bernardo Silva in the squad, and not giving Paz minutes would not be ideal for his current trajectory. It remains to be seen how Real Madrid approach this situation and whether they pay the money to bring Paz back to the Santiago Bernabeu next summer.

item.title: INTERVIEW: Owomoyela hails disciplinarian Kovač, debates how Dortmund can retain talents
item.description: INTERVIEW: Owomoyela hails disciplinarian Kovač, debates how Dortmund can retain talents MÜNCHEN ( Bulinews ) Former Borussia Dortmund defender Patrick Owomoyela is of the opinion that Niko Kovač has brought stability to the club since he was appointed as head coach just under two years ago. “Everybody knows Niko [Kovač] as a player, he has a high demand in discipline and in defensive structure first. That was him as a player and that’s where his focus lies as a coach as well," he informed Bulinews.com . “There have been a lot of critics suggesting that he is not able to develop good play with the ball. I don’t think so. It was just about changing Dortmund’s stability first and giving them the right placement. “This is what we have seen in the two years with Dortmund, now that he has stabilised the defence and added a few [new] players […] it’s still a project but he managed to create that solid foundation. “On top of that now, it’s about finding the right additions that are creative and do the right stuff with the ball. That’s not easy, especially when you’re not able to spend big money so he has to be creative. “That’s why they get a guy like [Kostas] Karetsas who wasn’t cheap, but BVB had to step back from other signings that were too expensive. This is what he was brought in to do and that’s why he got a new contract," he said. Time and again, one of Dortmund's biggest tailbacks is having to sell and replenish talent in a short space of time. Owomoyela knows this, but senses the trick to keeping them at BVB longer is by offering a sense of belief. “It’s difficult. You have to be successful and give these talents a promising future. Something they can see happening for them at the club. Of course, everybody wants to be successful, play Champions League and with their national teams. “At some point, they want to play for the biggest club whatever that is for those players. But to keep them at Borussia Dortmund, you have to show them something is possible here and so far, this season shows it is. “[Joane] Gadou is someone already that has played a lot, Karetsas has played a lot and is back [from injury]. These are young players; the season is looking good and maybe they believe something is possible and stick with Dortmund," the 46-year-old explained.

item.title: Man Utd ready for legal WAR with Real Madrid as teenage sensation JJ Gabriel goes AWOL to force transfer
item.description: JJ Gabriel Manchester United youth team - Getty Manchester United are bracing for a high-stakes legal confrontation with Real Madrid as teenage prodigy JJ Gabriel nears an exit from Old Trafford. The 16-year-old sensation has reportedly agreed to join the Spanish giants after effectively cutting ties with the Premier League side earlier this season. United frustrated by AWOL prodigy Gabriel stunned the Old Trafford hierarchy in September when he formally requested a transfer . The 16-year-old has not featured for the club since and completely severed communication, ignoring multiple attempts by United officials to make contact. Instead, the youngster relocated to Spain and has been maintaining his fitness independently in Castelldefels, Barcelona . His decision stems from growing impatience over a perceived lack of first-team opportunities . Furthermore, the attacker reportedly holds concerns regarding United's overall trajectory in recent seasons, leading him to conclude that his development requires a new environment. Madrid lead the chase for Gabriel A host of elite European clubs quickly circled the highly-rated forward. Bayern Munich, Paris Saint-Germain, and Barcelona all registered serious interest, but Real Madrid have ultimately won the race for his signature. Reports from Spain indicate Los Blancos have tabled a lucrative three-year contract . The proposed deal is understood to be worth in excess of £850,000 per season, orchestrated closely by his family and representative Ali Bharat. To facilitate a seamless transition to the continent, Gabriel recently secured a European Union passport following his 16th birthday in October. However, formal negotiations have yet to commence, with United officials receiving no direct contact from either the Spanish heavyweights or the player's entourage. The battle for fair compensation Despite Gabriel’s desire to depart, United still hold his playing registration and refuse to lose one of Europe’s premier talents for a nominal sum. The club feels deeply let down by the teenager's conduct, especially after investing heavily in his development since his arrival at Carrington in 2022. Under standard FIFA regulations, cross-border moves for academy players yield minimal training compensation, estimated at just £100,000 to £300,000. United argue this figure falls drastically short of Gabriel's true market value. Consequently, the Red Devils are prepared to escalate the matter through legal channels, as per Manchester Evening News . The youth transfer market has grown increasingly fierce, evidenced by domestic tribunals like Liverpool being ordered to pay Chelsea £2.8 million for Rio Ngumoha earlier this year. United will point to such precedents to demand an appropriate fee. A complex exit looms While Gabriel appears destined for the Bernabeu, an immediate resolution remains unlikely. item.title: Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence’s ‘relentless’ Liam Coen take that shows how he turned Jacksonville into a juggernaut
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence’s ‘relentless’ Liam Coen take that shows how he turned Jacksonville into a juggernaut appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville Jaguars kept rolling on Thursday night with a dominant 33-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens , and the star quarterback made sure head coach Liam Coen got his share of the credit. Speaking with the “Thursday Night Football” crew on Prime Video after the game , Lawrence was asked about Coen’s impact on the organization. Jacksonville is now 19-6 in the regular season since Coen took over. “Yeah, he’s great. I mean, he’s relentless the way he, you know, prepares, just the way he thinks. I think he’s a great leader for our team. You know, guys respond really well to, you know, how he leads. He’s got a lot of energy, a lot of enthusiasm, brings the juice every day. And then you see the things that we’re able to do offensively,” he said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) "He's relentless the way he prepares." Trevor Lawrence on how Liam Coen has improved this Jaguars team #TNFonPrime pic.twitter.com/gHhqykOj0M — NFL on Prime Video (@NFLonPrime) November 6, 2026 “He’s also really smart, has a great staff that he’s put together, and guys that are great coaches around us. And then I think, you know, the players are all bought into it,” Lawrence added. The 27-year-old also shared a funny story about his head coach. After settling for three second-half field goals, the Jaguars finally found the end zone again late in the fourth quarter on a Chris Rodriguez touchdown run. Lawrence joked that the team “might have to take a commercial flight home” if they had not scored. “He wanted that 700,” he said with a laugh. That late touchdown pushed Coen’s offense to 702 points through 25 games together. The turnaround under Coen has been impressive. Coen arrived in 2025 from the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, where he was offensive coordinator, and guided Jacksonville to a 13-4 record and an AFC South title . Lawrence finished fifth in MVP voting that year. This season, the Jaguars are 6-2 and look like one of the best teams in the AFC. Lawrence threw for 242 yards and a 50-yard touchdown to Parker Washington against the Ravens, and he now has 17 touchdowns to just four turnovers on the year. Traveling Jaguars fans even serenaded him with “MVP” chants in Baltimore. Jacksonville’s defense was just as impressive, holding Baltimore to 227 total yards and forcing three takeaways . With Lawrence and Coen clicking, the Jaguars have every reason to believe they can make a deep run this season. Related: Jaguars’ Trevor Lawrence showered with MVP chants in Baltimore after crushing Ravens Related: Jaguars are team to beat in the AFC after destroying Ravens to get to 6-2

item.title: Nick Saban Makes Exciting Personal News Heading Into Alabama vs. LSU Showdown
item.description: TUSCALOOSA, ALABAMA - SEPTEMBER 28: Former Alabama Crimson Tide head coach Nick Saban looks on before the game against the Georgia Bulldogs at Bryant-Denny Stadium on September 28, 2024 in Tuscaloosa, Alabama. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty Former Alabama head coach Nick Saban has launched a successful media career since leaving coaching after the 2023 season. He is currently an analyst on ESPN’s “College GameDay,” and he is now making a guest appearance on one of the biggest sports podcasts. Travis and Jason Kelce teased that Saban will appear on their podcast, “New Heights,” on Friday. The Kelce brothers are two of the most famous sibling duos in NFL history. Travis is currently a tight end for the Kansas City Chiefs, while Jason spent 13 years as a starting center for the Philadelphia Eagles and retired in 2023. Jason and Travis Almost Got a Chance to Face Saban in 2009 Travis and Jason both played college football at Cincinnati. Travis and Jason also had a chance to almost face Saban while a Bearcat in 2009. Cincinnati ended up playing Florida in the 2009 Sugar Bowl because the Gators lost to Alabama in the SEC title game and did not go on to play for the national championship. Alabama went on to beat Texas in the national championship game. If Florida had beaten Alabama in the SEC title game, Alabama likely would have played Cincinnati in the Sugar Bowl, and the Gators would have played Texas in the national championship. The Gators beat the Bearcats 51-24 in the last college football game Florida quarterback Tim Tebow ever played in. Tebow was out of eligibility after the 2009 season, and the Denver Broncos drafted him with the 25th overall pick in the 2010 NFL Draft. Saban coached in the 2008 Sugar Bowl after Alabama fell to Florida in the 2008 SEC title game, and the Crimson Tide fell to Utah, which was still part of the Mountain West Conference. Saban Coached Both LSU and Alabama It’s pretty cool that Saban will be on the podcast a day before the Alabama vs. LSU game, especially since he coached at both schools. Saban coached at LSU for five seasons from 2000 to 2004, finishing with a 48-16 record and winning the 2003 BCS National Championship. Saban then coached Alabama from 2007 to 2023, becoming one of the best college football coaches of all time and leading the Crimson Tide to six national championships: three in the BCS era and three in the College Football Playoff era. LSU and Alabama have a pretty big rivalry, and Saban coaching at both schools adds to it. Saban finished with a 13-5 record against LSU as Alabama head coach and even beat the Tigers 21-0 in the 2012 BCS National Championship Game. Alabama will travel to play LSU on Saturday, with a 3:30 p.m. ET kickoff. Both schools are 6-2, so this game could be a playoff-elimination matchup. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Nick Saban Makes Exciting Personal News Heading Into Alabama vs. LSU Showdown appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: ‘We’ve Got to Reconsider Some Stuff’ — Ex-NFL MVP Details the ‘Only Way’ Shedeur Sanders Could Start for Cleveland the Rest of the Season
item.description: ‘We’ve Got to Reconsider Some Stuff’ — Ex-NFL MVP Details the ‘Only Way’ Shedeur Sanders Could Start for Cleveland the Rest of the Season Shedeur Sanders might finally be getting his opportunity as a starter this season to prove he belongs under center for the Cleveland Browns. However, one start might not be enough to change his standing in the quarterback room. With Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol, Sanders is in line to make his first start of the season against the New Orleans Saints. According to Cam Newton, the second-year quarterback will need something special to convince Cleveland to reconsider its quarterback plans. Cam Newton Sets Benchmark for Shedeur Sanders to Keep Browns Starting QB Job Newton, the 2015 NFL MVP, three-time Pro Bowler and former Carolina Panthers quarterback, believes a big performance could significantly change the conversation surrounding Sanders’ future. Speaking on “4th&1 with Cam Newton,” he suggested that Sanders would need to deliver an exceptional offensive performance to have a realistic chance of keeping the starting role. “The stock could be hot,” Newton said . “The only way I see Shedeur Sanders starting for the rest of the season is if they exceed some type of benchmark that was set. Like, I think it was 300 yards plus. If they have a 400-yard offensive day, oh man, we’ve got to reconsider some stuff.” Sanders, for his part, is keeping it simple. “On my end, I just have to step up for the quarterback room, for the team, and do what I have to do,” he said at his Wednesday press conference. IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator This is not unfamiliar territory for the second-year quarterback. Sanders took over Cleveland’s offense last season after Dillon Gabriel sustained a concussion, starting the Browns’ final seven games of the campaign. Cleveland went 3-4 during his seven starts, with Sanders finishing his rookie season with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Those numbers leave plenty of room for improvement, but he now has a full offseason in Todd Monken’s offense behind him and has had additional time to develop chemistry with his potential targets. Deshaun Watson’s Inconsistent Numbers Give Sanders an Opening Newton’s proposed benchmark might sound demanding, but Watson’s performances this season offer some context for why Sanders could have an opportunity to make an impression. Through eight games, Watson has thrown for 1,806 yards, seven touchdowns, and three interceptions. He ranks 22nd in Pro Football Network’s QB Impact Score with a 70.3 grade, while his EPA per dropback sits around zero. But if Sanders delivers anything close to what Newton described, Cleveland may have a decision to make. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Where to watch Grizzlies vs. Thunder today: Channel, live stream, time, TV schedule for Friday NBA game
item.description: Where to watch Grizzlies vs. Thunder today: Channel, live stream, time, TV schedule for Friday NBA game originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . An enticing NBA Cup matchup will take place in Memphis Friday as the Grizzlies host the Thunder for a group stage showdown. This game will have many storylines to follow, but Ty Jerome will be a particularly interesting one. The Memphis guard is currently a top scorer in the league, and will be facing one of his former teams. Of course, the Grizzlies will also be looking to defend their undefeated 6-0 record as they continue through group play. Though the Thunder boast a 5-2 record at the moment, they are deep in an injury crisis that could have major implications for the rest of the season. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is still playing at MVP-caliber, but he has little backup without Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace or Alex Caruso. Who will score a group stage win? Here's everything you need to know about Grizzlies vs. Thunder today, including TV channel and streaming options for the NBA game. Where to watch Grizzlies vs. Thunder today TV channels: WATN ABC24 (Memphis), KSBI Channel 52 (OKC) Live streams: DAZN (Grizzlies) The Grizzlies-Thunder game will be televised locally by WATN ABC24 in Memphis, and KSBI Channel 52 in Oklahoma City. Those in the Memphis market can also watch live and on-demand with DAZN . item.content:encoded: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 24: Mateus Fernandes of Tottenham Hotspur celebrates their first goal with Dominic Solanke of Tottenham Hotspur and Mathys Tel of Tottenham Hotspur during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Chelsea FC and Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge on October 24, 2026 in London, United Kingdom. (Photo by Jacques Feeney/Offside/Offside via Getty Images) | Offside via Getty Images Good morning everyone and welcome to Fitzie’s Film and TV Reviews, where your hoddler-in-chief reviews all things he’s recently watches on screens big and small. It’s been a good while since we had a proper update on this, and I’ve watched a fair amount of television and film lately. I would say I’ve enjoyed most, but few have had a major impression on me. Nobody Wants this, series 3: The Netflix rom-com hit starring Kristin Bell and Adam Brody returns to its kinetic pace after a been-there-done-that second series. But it doesn’t come from the leads who star as Esther and Noah, respectively, who settle into moving together nicely after Esther decides to convert to Judaism. At this point in a relationship, it’s a little common for things to be steady, not exhilerating. But fear not, Timothy Simmons and Justin Lupe more than make up for that as Sasha (Noah’s brother) and Morgan (Esther’s sister). The former navigates a divorce, and the second appears a little stuck. The final four episodes bring us back to the heights of the first series, it just comes from a different source. 3.5 out of 5 Fitzies Taskmaster, series 22: Even bad Taskmaster is good Taskmaster . I think that’s the case with Series 22, where the tasks felt cumbersome and the contestants didn’t quite seem to gel. This series featured Chloe Petts, Isy Suttie, Matt Lucas, Nina Conti and Richard Ayoade. I really wanted to like this more than I did because I love the show. But after a brilliant three-series run from 19-21, this feels like a step back. 3 out of 5 Fitzies Last One Laughing Halloween: Speaking of new series, there was a Halloween special for Last One Laughing . The premise is simple: A group of comedians are locked in a room for several hours and aren’t allowed to laugh. Last one standing wins. There are a few standouts in this special like Jack Dee and the spookmaster himself Reece Sheersmith. I think those two, along with returnee Lou Sanders, engaged with the concept the most. I think a couple other contestants played much more “defensive” which is much less enjoyable to watch. A decent four-episode run, but I won’t be returning to it. 3 out of 5 Fitzies Conspiracy : Think 12 Angry Men , but this time it’s a group deciding on Nazi Germany’s final solution. It’s a harrowing and shocking depiction of the process, where the dialogue and points of conflict focused on the morality of killing millions, but the measures on how to do so. Kenneth Branagh and Stanley Tucci were incredible playing the two men leading the meeting, while Colin Firth an interesting foil. Although we of course know his decisions and beliefs were just as deplorable. I sat through the 90-minute film aghast at the coldness in how these decisions were made, and left stunned the film was based on the one remaining piece of evidence it happened. 5 out of 5 Fitzies The West Wing : Classic American television and it took me way too long to get into it. I’m currently on Season 5, but have seen enough to weigh judgment. Everyone in this is remarkable, although I find a little humour in the end of every season having some over-the-top dramatic storyline. You think the West Wingers would’ve figured out to stay indoors by the time Episodes 22 roll around. 5 out of 5 Fitzies Survivor, series 51: I don’t really know why I’m watching this. It’s mostly background noise at this point. I had some hope after a successful all-returnee Series 50, but I’m sick of people hyping themselves up. It’s still early on so things could get better, but it’s falling flat for something that’s supposed to return the game more to its roots. Two pieces of advice for the show-runners: Go back to the old challenges, and let’s get our 39 days back. 2 out of 5 Fitzies Bugonia : I’m not a big fan of Yorgos Lanthimos, but I wanted to watch something a little creepy and unconventional this Halloween. This film stars Jesse Plemons and Aidan Delbis, two men who kidnap a powerful CEO (Emma Stone) under the belief that she’s an alien come to harm the earth. There is some fascinating dialogue and the torture scenes are difficult to sit through. I think Stone and Plemons did an incredible job in their characters, but for me this is another film where I’m asking what the point was. I understand Lanthimos loves dark humour and dives into absurdities etc, but I don’t really understand the point of that here. Maybe I should just stop watching him as I’m clearly not who he’s making films for. 3.5 out of 5 Fitzies Ftizie’s track of the day: I Wanna Rock, by Twisted Sister And now for your links: The Athletic ($$) : “Were we wrong about Archie Gray not being a right-back?” The Guardian : “‘In moments of pain, football comes together’: Spain says goodbye to Jesús de Miguel” BBC : “A bitter end for Ronaldo – the icon who transformed Portugal”

item.title: Wolff admits Mercedes shortcomings as he defends Russell after title defeat
item.description: Toto Wolff has defended George Russell following Kimi Antonelli’s championship triumph in Mexico, admitting Mercedes have not always given the Briton the car to perform this season. While Antonelli celebrated becoming the youngest Formula 1 champion in history last weekend, George Russell left early after the disappointment of missing out on the championship. Speaking in Mercedes' preview for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, Wolff stressed that Russell's season had been affected by circumstances beyond his control. Wolff backs Russell after Antonelli’s championship success Speaking in Mercedes' preview for this weekend's race in Brazil, Wolff said: “Mexico was a special weekend for Kimi and the team. Winning the World Championship is an incredible achievement, particularly at this stage of his career, and he thoroughly deserves the moment. “For George, there is natural disappointment. He has been hard on himself but he has driven at an incredibly high level this season and shown again the quality we know he has. “There have been circumstances out of his control that haven't always fallen his way, and we have not always given him the car to perform. Nevertheless, the way he has continued to push and contributed to the team says so much about him.” Mercedes turn attention to securing both championships With the drivers' championship settled, Mercedes head to Interlagos with another title still to secure. If Mercedes outscore Ferrari by three points, or more this weekend, they will win the constructors' championship. “Our focus, though, has already moved to São Paulo. We came into this season wanting to fight for both championships and there is still a job left to finish,” Wolff continued. “The teams' title is about the performance of the entire operation, both at the track and back in Brackley and Brixworth, and securing it would mean a great deal to all of us. “Nothing is won yet, though. Interlagos is always a demanding weekend and there is little margin for error. We need to execute strongly from the first session and put ourselves in the best possible position to bring home both titles this season.”

item.title: UTSA 'manhandled' in road loss to FAU as American title hopes take a hit
item.description: BOCA RATON, FL - NOVEMBER 05: Florida Atlantic Owls running back Leonard Farrow (5) breaks free for a long run in the first half during the game between UTSA and FAU on Thursday, November 5, 2026 at Flagler Credit Union Stadium in Boca Raton, FL (Photo by Peter Joneleit/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) (Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) BOCA RATON, Fla. - Leaving the field after a lopsided loss to Florida Atlantic, UTSA coach Jeff Traylor returned to a locker room that he described as disappointed, embarrassed and disgusted. The Roadrunners entered the night on the fringe of the national top 25 with everything in front of them, remaining in strong position for an American Conference championship and a College Football Playoff berth for as long as they could keep their winning streak going. Instead, UTSA was overpowered and outplayed on both sides of the ball, allowing the highest point total of Traylor's tenure in a 60-29 road rout Thursday. "We didn't give our kids a great plan as a staff. They gave their guys a better plan than we did," Traylor said. "So, it starts with the staff, but up front, we got manhandled on both sides of the ball." UTSA coach Jeff Traylor after a 60-29 loss at FAU: "We didn't give our kids a great plan as a staff. They gave their guys a better plan than we did. So it starts with the staff. But up front, we got manhandled on both sides of the ball." https://t.co/T9GUdUJHlo - Greg Luca (@GregLuca) November 6, 2026 The loss drops the Roadrunners to 7-2 on the year with a 4-1 record in the American Conference, snapping a five-game winning streak. UTSA remains in contention for the league title, as North Texas is the lone unbeaten at 4-0, and Memphis is the only other one-loss team at 4-1. But the path to a College Football Playoff spot as the highest-ranked team in the Group of Six became much more perilous. UTSA entered the night receiving votes in both the Associated Press and coaches polls, joining the conversation with Boise State and New Mexico as the best in the Group of Six. The Roadrunners will now need both of those teams and perhaps a few others to drop games down the stretch. "It's a new challenge now," UTSA quarterback Owen McCown said. "We'll see how our team responds. I know they'll respond the right way." UTSA's defense had been spotty in stretches all season, entering the night ranked just outside the top 100 nationally in total defense at 391.5 yards per game. But the Roadrunners had usually managed to find success in one aspect or another, often taking away an opponent's biggest strength and forcing them to play out of rhythm. The Owls' up-tempo, air raid attack entered the night ranked in the top five in the country in passing and in the bottom 20 in rushing, but Traylor said he was "pretty shocked" to see how heavily the Owls committed to the run, as FAU exploded for 339 yards on the ground. FAU averaged 6.9 yards per rush, led by running back Leonard Farrow with 12 carries for 126 yards

The Roadrunners entered the night on the fringe of the national top 25 with everything in front of them, remaining in strong position for an American Conference championship and a College Football Playoff berth for as long as they could keep their winning streak going. Instead, UTSA was overpowered and outplayed on both sides of the ball, allowing the highest point total of Traylor's tenure in a 60-29 road rout Thursday. "We didn't give our kids a great plan as a staff. They gave their guys a better plan than we did," Traylor said. "So, it starts with the staff, but up front, we got manhandled on both sides of the ball." UTSA coach Jeff Traylor after a 60-29 loss at FAU: "We didn't give our kids a great plan as a staff. They gave their guys a better plan than we did. So it starts with the staff. But up front, we got manhandled on both sides of the ball." https://t.co/T9GUdUJHlo - Greg Luca (@GregLuca) November 6, 2026 The loss drops the Roadrunners to 7-2 on the year with a 4-1 record in the American Conference, snapping a five-game winning streak. UTSA remains in contention for the league title, as North Texas is the lone unbeaten at 4-0, and Memphis is the only other one-loss team at 4-1. But the path to a College Football Playoff spot as the highest-ranked team in the Group of Six became much more perilous. UTSA entered the night receiving votes in both the Associated Press and coaches polls, joining the conversation with Boise State and New Mexico as the best in the Group of Six. The Roadrunners will now need both of those teams and perhaps a few others to drop games down the stretch. "It's a new challenge now," UTSA quarterback Owen McCown said. "We'll see how our team responds. I know they'll respond the right way." UTSA's defense had been spotty in stretches all season, entering the night ranked just outside the top 100 nationally in total defense at 391.5 yards per game. But the Roadrunners had usually managed to find success in one aspect or another, often taking away an opponent's biggest strength and forcing them to play out of rhythm. The Owls' up-tempo, air raid attack entered the night ranked in the top five in the country in passing and in the bottom 20 in rushing, but Traylor said he was "pretty shocked" to see how heavily the Owls committed to the run, as FAU exploded for 339 yards on the ground. FAU averaged 6.9 yards per rush, led by running back Leonard Farrow with 12 carries for 126 yards and a score. "We knew everything coming in," UTSA defensive lineman Jeremiah Bailey said. "They were more prepared, got the best of us tonight." The Owls' passing attack was effective when needed, as well, racking up 224 yards as FAU became the first team to eclipse 200 yards both through the air and on the ground against UTSA this year. BOCA RATON, FL - NOVEMBER 05: Florida Atlantic Owls tight end Antonio Johnson (1) rushes for a touchdown int he first half during the game between UTSA and FAU on Thursday, November 5, 2026 at Flagler Credit Union Stadium in Boca Raton, FL (Photo by Peter Joneleit/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) (Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Quarterback Caden Veltkamp hit 17 of 25 passes for 210 yards with four touchdowns, including three to star wideout Easton Messer. "It always starts up front," Traylor said. "Their O-line manhandled us." That physical disadvantage was evident on the other side, too, as Traylor said UTSA's offensive line "couldn't protect our quarterback." McCown completed 20 of 35 passes for 265 yards with three touchdowns but was sacked six times as the Roadrunners faced consistent pressure. "I have full trust in those guys up front on the O-line," McCown said. "I just don't think they played as good as they wanted to tonight, and that's all right. It's part of football. It's more important to see the response." UTSA's rushing attack was also held to 136 yards at an average of 3.8 yards per carry, and FAU often pulled a safety up closer to the line of scrimmage to limit the Roadrunners' ground game. That put more of a burden on UTSA's receivers to beat their defenders, and Traylor said the Roadrunners targets "weren't winning on press coverage," forcing McCown to hold onto the ball longer. BOCA RATON, FL - NOVEMBER 05: *UTSA Roadrunners quarterback Owen McCown (2) makes a pass attempt in the first half during the game between UTSA and FAU on Thursday, November 5, 2026 at Flagler Credit Union Stadium in Boca Raton, FL (Photo by Peter Joneleit/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) (Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) "We've got to get receivers open," Traylor said. "As a coaching staff, we've got to do a better job, and receivers have to get open and win some of those downfield throws. That's really it." After having a few extra days to heal up through the open week, an array of Roadrunners went down to injuries on Thursday, and Traylor said UTSA "lost some great players tonight." The extent of most of the knocks remains unknown, Traylor said, but UTSA's ability to shuffle the depth chart where needed is "going to be the biggest deal" as the Roadrunners look to regroup. North Texas will present a very similar challenge, entering the week ranked atop the FBS in total offense at 539.6 yards per game. A win vaults UTSA back into a first-place tie atop the American, and McCown expects the group to answer the challenge. "I hope as a team this puts a little chip on our shoulder going into a really big game next week," McCown said. "We're still in this hunt. It's the top of the conference, but we're having to play a really good team next week in the Dome in North Texas. So, we have to respond the right way. I know we will." item.title: 'Putting his doubters in their place' - Rooney lands pundit of year award
item.description: Wayne Rooney has transitioned to broadcasting following a managerial career with Derby County, DC United, Birmingham City and Plymouth Argyle [Getty Images] "I like a lot of them artists, but I thought it was crap." Wayne Rooney's assessment of the 2026 World Cup final half-time show - delivered live on BBC Television - was blunt. The show, which featured Madonna, BTS, Shakira and Justin Bieber, ran to 27 minutes and 22 seconds. Rooney, who played at three World Cups for England, was unimpressed. It caught some - including fellow pundit Joe Hart - by surprise. But Rooney's plain-speaking and sense of humour through the tournament had connected with viewers. On Thursday, the former Manchester United and England captain was named pundit of the year at the Broadcast Sport Awards. Rooney, 41, was presented with the prestigious prize in front of 650 people from the sports television industry at a ceremony in London. "I didn't realise how tough it was going to be when I first started doing it," said Rooney about transitioning from football to broadcasting. "I've always been my own biggest critic. And even now I need to improve, I need to be better. "It's a lot of hard work." Rooney's move to broadcasting after a stellar playing career - followed by a testing stint as a manager - has not always been smooth. His debut as a full-time pundit on Match of the Day in August 2025 divided opinion, with one fan writing on social media: "Just because you have done something, does not automatically make you good to talk/explain and teach others well." Guardian journalist Paul MacInnes was more upbeat about Rooney's debut. "He's articulate, and on Saturday night was able to conjure up the right word when you could see he was looking for it," he wrote. "He is tactically insightful and has a wealth of experience to draw from too." As a player, Rooney learned from managers including Sir Alex Ferguson and David Moyes, and won the Champions League, Europa League, Premier League (five times), FA Cup and League Cup (three times). He was not always the most articulate in his post-match interviews. As a pundit, he has found his voice. In an attempt to better himself as a broadcaster, Rooney has sought feedback and advice from experienced television executives, as well as other players-turned-pundits including Alan Shearer, Danny Murphy, Hart and Micah Richards. "I do look at the other pundits who have been there a long time," added Rooney. "I see how they do it. I enjoy it, it keeps me involved in football." "He is tactically insightful and has a wealth of experience to draw from too." As a player, Rooney learned from managers including Sir Alex Ferguson and David Moyes, and won the Champions League, Europa League, Premier League (five times), FA Cup and League Cup (three times). "I do look at the other pundits who have been there a long time," added Rooney. "I see how they do it. I enjoy it, it keeps me involved in football." Asked about dealing with criticism from people watching him on TV, Rooney responded: "You do see it. "It drives me to be better. I always feel when I do something I want to do better and be the best I can." Paul Stretford, Rooney's long-serving agent, said people should not be surprised by what his client can achieve. "It is no surprise to me that Wayne has continued to put his doubters in their place with his football intelligence and straightforward manner," added Stretford. "Time and time again as a player he was able to raise his game to incredible levels. "They should also not be surprised at his drive and ambition to be the best that he can possibly be. And he does this with a combination of intelligence and humility." Philip Bernie, head of BBC Sport events, said Rooney had shown a "great willingness to learn and determination to improve" as a broadcaster. "Wayne is also a very likeable guy, a proper team player, with no ego on display," he added. As well as developing chemistry with his fellow pundits, Rooney has changed his appearance after committing to a healthier lifestyle through a fitness regime which involves games of padel and boxing training. "Like anyone who cares about their job, Wayne had to work hard - to learn skills around analysis and delivery - and he's improved so much in a short time," said Alex Kay-Jelski, director of BBC Sport. "Micah and Joe alongside him at the World Cup were perfect team-mates - three equals - and you'll be seeing more of them together on the BBC in coming seasons." Their chemistry was obvious in the summer, particularly when they swapped their microphones for oars after an erroneous Rooney prediction. He pledged to row down the River Mersey if Norway beat Brazil, and when they did, he confirmed on air he would adapt the challenge to do it in the United States. That led to him, Hart and Richards to take to the Hudson River in New York. "Wayne deserves this so much," added Kay-Jelski. "He's a great mix of incredibly clever, funny in a self-deprecating manner and likeable. "From a BBC side he's easy to work with, treats everyone the same whether they're a former team-mate or starting out in a junior position, and his words carry real weight." item.title: ‘I have been subject to a lot of hate’: RCB star reveals how fans trolled him whenever Shubman Gill hit a ton
item.description: Venkatesh Iyer has opened up about the prolonged online backlash he faced from Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR) supporters following the franchise's decision to retain him while releasing Shubman Gill ahead of IPL 2022. The Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) batter revealed that the criticism has continued over the years, with fans still targeting him whenever Gill scores a century. Gill was released by KKR ahead of the 2022 season and subsequently became one of the three players drafted by the newly formed Gujarat Titans (GT), who secured his services for Rs 8 crore alongside Hardik Pandya and Rashid Khan. Speaking in a podcast with Aakash Chopra, Venkatesh recalled how KKR supporters have repeatedly brought up the franchise's decision, making him a target of social media trolling. "I have been subject to a lot of hate for a long time. Even till date, if Shubman is getting a hundred; you go to a KKR page, people would be commenting, 'in search of gold, we lost a diamond' and all of that stuff," Venkatesh said. The 31-year-old also discussed his situation ahead of the IPL 2026 auction, particularly after KKR decided to release him. He revealed that he had even approached franchise co-owner Shah Rukh Khan in the hope of a change in the decision. "I had kept an hankerchief on the side. I even asked Shah Rukh sir," he said. KKR had spent Rs 23.75 crore to buy Venkatesh back ahead of the 2025 season. However, following his release, the all-rounder admitted that he had already moved on mentally and was not even considering a return to the franchise during the 2026 auction. "I didn't even think about the pay cut. I had already started thinking, 'Okay, it's not going to be purple'," he said. Venkatesh was eventually signed by defending champions RCB, where he got an opportunity to experience a completely different fan culture. The batter was particularly struck by the devotion of Bengaluru supporters and described their connection with the franchise as something he had never witnessed before. "You won't believe this, but I saw people actually worshipping the RCB jersey before matches. This was something different. Fandom at a different level," Venkatesh recalled. His initial days at RCB involved spending time on the bench before he was introduced as an Impact Substitute after the team suffered an early collapse in the batting order. He responded with an unbeaten 29 off 15 deliveries, helping RCB reach 201/8, although the team eventually lost the match. Venkatesh later delivered another impressive performance against Punjab Kings, remaining unbeaten on 73 off 40 balls. He ended the season with 209 runs from seven matches at an average of 52.25, playing his part in RCB's successful campaign as the franchise secured its second IPL title in a row. 135591640

item.title: From playing against Messi & Ronaldo to non-league
item.description: Fernando Forestieri has gone from playing in the top leagues in Italy and Spain to signing for Oxford City [Oxford City] A Saturday afternoon in October at the Hebburn Sports and Social Ground, Tyne & Wear. Some Hebburn Town fans are already heading for the exits as Oxford City, 3-0 up in the 81st minute, send on their new signing. Fernando Forestieri has shared pitches with Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo and Zlatan Ibrahimovic, and played in front 72,000 fans at Real Madrid's iconic Bernabeu Stadium. On this occasion, down in English football's sixth tier, there are 873 supporters present to witness Oxford City's new Argentine number 15 come on for his debut. "It was like a tennis match, the ball going one way one second, then the other way the next," Forestieri, 36, told BBC Sport after his new club, nicknamed the Hoops, secured a seventh win in 11 games to sit third in National League North. On Friday, Oxford City host Leicester City in the first round of the FA Cup (19:45 GMT), with former Watford and Sheffield Wednesday forward Forestieri looking to inspire the non-league club to a famous win over the League One Foxes. It is 10 years since Leicester famously won the Premier League title. In the same season Forestieri was helping Sheffield Wednesday reach the Championship play-off final, where the Owls lost to Hull City at Wembley. "There's a big gap between what Leicester did 10 years ago and where they are now," he said. "Why can't Oxford City cause an upset? This is what the FA Cup is all about." Forestieri ready for fresh challenge at Oxford City Forestieri encountered Barcelona, Messi and Ibrahimovic while playing for Malaga in Spain's top flight in 2009-10. Meanwhile, he shared the same pitch with Ronaldo as recently as five years ago when Juventus played Forestieri's Udinese team in Serie A. "You never forget being on the same pitch with these big players," added Forestieri, whose CV includes scoring against Inter Milan for Siena in 2008. "Messi, Ronaldo, Ibrahimovic... unbelievable skills. "I'm very lucky. Being that close to them you remember their first touch, their vision." Forestieri grew up playing football on the streets of Rosario - the same city in Argentina Messi was born - and idolised Diego Maradona. When Maradona died in 2020, Forestieri wrote a tribute to the 1986 Argentina World Cup winner on the back of his Udinese shirt. "Growing up in Argentina, everyone pretended to be Diego," he said. "He was a hero to everyone. On every corner of every street someone painted his face on a wall." Talking about his childhood, Forestieri said: "I was born poor, born with nothing. "I lived with my mum and dad and two brothers. The five of us slept in one room." Rosario was a dangerous area and Forestieri's brother, Maximiliano, was shot and wounded. Some Hebburn Town fans are already heading for the exits as Oxford City, 3-0 up in the 81st minute, send on their new signing. Fernando Forestieri has shared pitches with Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo and Zlatan Ibrahimovic, and played in front 72,000 fans at Real Madrid's iconic Bernabeu Stadium. On this occasion, down in English football's sixth tier, there are 873 supporters present to witness Oxford City's new Argentine number 15 come on for his debut. "It was like a tennis match, the ball going one way one second, then the other way the next," Forestieri, 36, told BBC Sport after his new club, nicknamed the Hoops, secured a seventh win in 11 games to sit third in National League North. On Friday, Oxford City host Leicester City in the first round of the FA Cup (19:45 GMT), with former Watford and Sheffield Wednesday forward Forestieri looking to inspire the non-league club to a famous win over the League One Foxes. It is 10 years since Leicester famously won the Premier League title. In the same season Forestieri was helping Sheffield Wednesday reach the Championship play-off final, where the Owls lost to Hull City at Wembley. "There's a big gap between what Leicester did 10 years ago and where they are now," he said. "Why can't Oxford City cause an upset? This is what the FA Cup is all about." Forestieri ready for fresh challenge at Oxford City Forestieri encountered Barcelona, Messi and Ibrahimovic while playing for Malaga in Spain's top flight in 2009-10. Meanwhile, he shared the same pitch with Ronaldo as recently as five years ago when Juventus played Forestieri's Udinese team in Serie A. "You never forget being on the same pitch with these big players," added Forestieri, whose CV includes scoring against Inter Milan for Siena in 2008. "Messi, Ronaldo, Ibrahimovic... unbelievable skills. "I'm very lucky. Being that close to them you remember their first touch, their vision." Forestieri grew up playing football on the streets of Rosario - the same city in Argentina Messi was born - and idolised Diego Maradona. When Maradona died in 2020, Forestieri wrote a tribute to the 1986 Argentina World Cup winner on the back of his Udinese shirt. "Growing up in Argentina, everyone pretended to be Diego," he said. "He was a hero to everyone. On every corner of every street someone painted his face on a wall." Talking about his childhood, Forestieri said: "I was born poor, born with nothing. "I lived with my mum and dad and two brothers. The five of us slept in one room." Rosario was a dangerous area and Forestieri's brother, Maximiliano, was shot and wounded. "Thankfully he survived," said Forestieri, who was part of the academies of famed Argentine clubs Newell's Old Boys and Boca Juniors. Aged 16, he moved to Italy and quickly made his senior debut for Genoa. He qualified to play for Italy through his grandfather and turned out for the Azzurri at youth levels. Twenty years after his senior debut for Genoa, and after recent spells in Malaysia and Cyprus, he is still playing - albeit in non-league, after returning to England following the birth of his third son, Luciano. Forestieri (left) aged 18, in action for Siena against AC Milan's Andrea Pirlo in 2008 [Getty Images] So, how did his move to Oxford City come about? Forestieri was at Watford at the same time as Hoops boss Ross Jenkins, while Oxford City assistant manager Paul Robinson is also a former Hornets player. He trained with the PFA as part of their pre-season programme for players without a club before getting a call from Robinson. "Robbo said: 'why you don't come here to help us? We'll help you to become fit'," explained Forestieri. "For me this is a big change. But I'm so happy to be at Oxford City. They are an ambitious club and I want to help them as much as I can." Forestieri paid tribute to Diego Maradona on the back of his Udinese shirt following the death of the Argentina legend in 2020 [Getty Images] The player, who is also taking his coaching badges, lives in north London with his wife, Andria, and their two other sons Santiago, aged nine, and Maximiliano, aged six. "I still have passion for football," he added. "Whenever I'm walking in the park with Santiago and we see someone playing football, we stop and join in. That's how much I still love football." Since making his debut against Hebburn, Forestieri has appeared in league games against Marine, Merthyr and South Shields. After the money-spinning Leicester tie, which is expected to attract a 3,500 sell-out crowd, Oxford City - who sit second in National League North - return to the north-east to play Darlington in a league match next Tuesday. "You need to listen to your body when you reach 36," said Forestieri. "But I'm lucky to be still playing and that a club still wants me to play for them." item.title: A Scottish influence has transformed New Zealand – but can the Scots finally beat the All Blacks?
item.description: The New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie took plenty from his three years at the Glasgow Warriors but it is the chuckles that he remembers most fondly. “The Scottish are funny people and I haven't laughed as much in any environment as much as I have in my time here,” Rennie explained back in 2020 after embarking on what proved an ill-fated stint with Australia. “I've loved the people and I've loved our time here. It's been special, we'll miss it.” Dave Rennie spent three years at Glasgow (Getty) Perhaps it is no surprise, then, that there has been such a strong Scottish influence at the heart of his project to restore the All Blacks ’ spirit. Mike Blair won 85 caps at scrum half and captained Scotland 14 times; until deciding he rather preferred life overseeing attack, it appeared he was being groomed as Gregor Townsend ’s successor in the highest coaching office in the land. Instead, he and Rennie return to Murrayfield with a New Zealand side in a phase of reinvention or rediscovery – re-finding the tenets that made them great and forging perhaps the world’s most outstanding attack. It has proved a natural fit. Blair has admitted to feeling a degree of impostor syndrome when he first came into All Blacks camp earlier this year, but has found the squad highly receptive to his methods. He has done excellent work, too, getting a tune out of a series of playmakers and associated parts through a demanding itinerary. Unbeaten so far in the Nations Championship having overcome France, Italy and Ireland in July, they carry confidence from two professional performances against the Wallabies last month. “We're in a good place, I think,” Blair said this week. “We’re pleased with what we did against Australia but we're also aware that playing Scotland at Murrayfield is a really big challenge. It's another good opportunity to show the growth in our game.” Scotland struggled to get close to New Zealand during the playing days of Mike Blair (far left) (Getty) The former scrum half made a self-deprecating crack that he’d already contributed to a few All Blacks wins over Scotland this week but his own playing days do serve as a reminder of how this challenge has changed for the tourists. Back when their attack coach wore the thistle, the result was a foregone conclusion; in four meetings with the All Blacks as a player, Blair only got within 20 points once. "When I played, New Zealand played their second-string team. They gave guys opportunity against us," he admitted. ”Times have changed from that.” The last four meetings have been decided by eight points or fewer. Scotland will rue missed opportunities in at least two of those, including last year – having hauled the game back to level pegging from 17-0 down, Townsend’s side could not sustain their effort.
